episodes.156294: Interaction between eastward propagating shortwave over Gulf of Mexico and stationary frontal boundary draped across the north/central Florida peninsula produces a MCS that affects the Nature Coast and central peninsula, producing a damaging wind gust.
episodes.156766: A front lifted north from central FL during the afternoon as a mid level impulse passed overhead. These features combined with diurnal instability produced a few strong to marginally severe storms.
episodes.156767: A front was draped across north-central Florida. Elevated instability on the north side of the front under a passing mid level impulse produced a severe storm that produced large hail over Flagler county in the morning. A stronger cell in the afternoon produced a weak tornado in Marion county.
episodes.156768: A front was draped across north-central Florida. Elevated instability on the north side of the front under a passing mid level impulse produced a severe storm that produced large hail over Flagler county in the morning. A stronger cell in the afternoon produced a weak tornado in Marion county.
episodes.156975: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed inland over Flagler County near a stationary front, then dropped quickly southeast. Strong winds and hail up to ping-pong ball size occurred along the coast near the county line, then crossed into the Atlantic.
episodes.156981: An isolated severe thunderstorm developed over Flagler County near a stationary front. The storm move quickly southeast along the Flagler-Volusia County line and produced large hail just south of the county line, in Ormond Beach.
episodes.158168: A few thunderstorms developed across eastern Hidalgo through Willacy County during the early morning hours on April 18th. Environmental conditions favored strong-to-marginally-severe storms across the area. A few intensified to the point of producing hail, with reports of hail up to the size of nickels observed in Willacy County. Storms quickly moved offshore later that morning.

The NWS confirmed a EF1 tornado touchdown on the westside of Ocala. The tornado moved to the east and produced structural wind damage. Plastic signs and street signs were twisted and ripped out of the ground. A large warehouse was damaged along State Road 40 east of Interstate 75. Power lines were downed and a large live oak tree was blown down. Peak wind were near 110 mph.
